Subject: Redlines - MSA + On‑Prem/VPC Addendum

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and infrastructure teams reviewed Redwood's MSA and we have a few redlines focused on Private deployment rights and an addendum for on‑prem/VPC installs. Key asks attached (FinCo_MSA_Redlines.docx):

- License scope: explicit right to install and run the software in our VPCs and on‑prem data centers, incl. ability to create immutable backups and DR replicas.
- Deployment rights: we want the ability to run in multiple regions (US/EU) and to provision additional nodes without renegotiation.
- Audit & verification: annual security audit rights (third party), plus access to limited runtime telemetry for compliance.
- Escrow-like request: in the event of Redwood insolvency or long‑term support cessation, we request access to a recovery package (source or build artifacts) via an escrow agent.
- KMS/HSM: compatibility with our customer‑managed KMS and ability to hold keys in our HSMs.

We recognize some of these are significant. Could you confirm Redwood's positions or provide counter‑language? I've copied procurement for contracting timelines — they are targeting an April go‑live.

Attachments: FinCo_MSA_Redlines.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Angela Soto

Folks — I pulled the redlines and sketched negotiation positions. Topline suggestions:

1) License scope / deployment rights
- We can grant a non‑exclusive, worldwide sublicensable right to install and run the specified Redwood runtime in Customer controlled infra (VPC/on‑prem) for the Term. Limit scope to "runtime binaries and configuration" rather than full source.
- Limit the automatic scale entitlement: allow customer to run within an agreed instance/host count or within an agreed performance tier; additional capacity should be addendum/PO.

2) Audit & verification
- Accept annual SOC2/ISO attestation and permit a single third‑party security audit per year with reasonable notice (30 days) and scope limits (no product source disclosure, read‑only access to logs/telemetry agreed in schedule).
- For runtime telemetry, provide a pre‑approved set of logs/metrics via our Console and limited API export; deny full access to raw key material or internal kernels.

3) Escrow‑like requests
- We won’t provide source code as a general matter. Offer a source escrow release mechanism with a recognized escrow agent triggered by limited events (bankruptcy, acquisition where support is discontinued) and tightly scoped release conditions. Alternatively, provide a documented build artifact bundle + runtime container images + dependencies under escrow.
- Require escrow agreement and associated fees to be mutually agreed.

4) KMS/HSM
- Support integration with customer KMS/HSM for keys used for data encryption in transit and at rest; require validated compatibility and a supported integration guide.

5) Changes to Agreement
- Suggest a focused Redwood Private Addendum that captures these operational items; keep MSA unchanged except to reference the addendum and audit schedule.

Questions for Sales: do we have existing customers with escrow arrangements? Dev — any technical constraints on delivering build artifact bundles vs full source? Vivek — any security showstoppers?

Lauren Bishop
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Lauren — technical notes:

- Deliverables: we can produce a reproducible build artifact bundle (compiled binaries, container images, pinned dependencies, build scripts) that allows FinCo to run the service without needing live Redwood support. This is preferable to full source escrow for IP reasons.
- Keys: we support BYOK integrations (customer KMS) for data encryption at rest and in transit; we will document the supported KMS providers and the HSM configuration matrix.
- Scale: auto‑scaling beyond an agreed throughput tier may require a new license tier; we can propose a flat headroom (e.g., +25% over baseline) for burst capacity included.
- Telemetry: we can export aggregated metrics and sampling of traces; raw token streams or prompt history cannot be provided.

Dev Patel

Agree with Lauren/Dev. Few security caveats to include in counter‑proposal:

- Audit scope: audits are fine but must be performed by a mutually agreed 3P and exclude proprietary code review. Any on‑site or remote audits should be limited to logs, configuration, and runtime behavior; we reserve the right to redact sensitive implementation details.
- Escrow contents: deliver encrypted runtime artifacts and build instructions; escrow release only on insolvency or when we fail to provide reasonable support for a sustained period (e.g., 120 days). No unrestricted release of full source.
- Operational security: require customer to maintain hardened infrastructure and follow the Redwood deployment checklist; we will not accept liability for customer‑side misconfigurations.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security Engineering
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Redlines - MSA + On‑Prem/VPC Addendum

Hi Angela — appreciate the clear redlines. Attached is a Redwood Private Addendum draft (Redwood_Private_Addendum_v1.docx) that incorporates the positions our legal and security teams outlined. High‑level summary of our position:

1) Deployment rights: Redwood will grant a non‑exclusive right to install and operate the Redwood runtime (binaries and configuration) in FinCo controlled VPCs/on‑prem infra for the Term. Deployment in EU regions is permitted; changes to global region scope require notice. Additional capacity beyond the agreed baseline will be handled via a capacity addendum or PO.

2) Audit & telemetry: FinCo may perform one third‑party security audit per 12 months with 30 days' notice; scope is limited to runtime/configuration and logs we expressly make available. Redwood will provide SOC2/ISO summary reports under NDA.

3) Escrow/recovery: Redwood cannot disclose unrestricted source code. We can place an encrypted recovery bundle (container images, reproducible build artifacts, pinned dependencies and deployment scripts) with an independent escrow agent. Release to FinCo is limited to defined release events (broadly insolvency, cessation of support for >120 days) and governed by an escrow agreement. Any escrow fees to be borne by FinCo unless otherwise agreed.

4) KMS/HSM: We support customer‑managed KMS integration; we’ll share our integration guide and a compatibility matrix.

We’re happy to walk through the proposed addendum in a short call. If this direction is acceptable, I’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope with the addendum and the MSA reference changes for signature. Given your April timeline, can we aim for a 3/10 signature target?

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/example123
